bash.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.
bash.name: bash

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

browser_exec.description: Drive a real browser by running Python in the session's sandbox, for JavaScript pages, logins, forms and clicks (for plain reading, prefer fetching the page). Start code with a one-line comment naming the step in plain words (e.g. `# Searching the catalogue for paper towels`). Batch a whole sub-procedure (navigate, wait, extract, act) into one call, and print only what you need: stdout is the result. STATE: the browser (its tabs, cookies and current page) persists across calls; Python variables do not (each call is a fresh interpreter). The folder $BROWSER_WORKSPACE (`.githi/browser` in the workspace, also `WORKSPACE`) persists: for many items, append each batch to a JSON or CSV file there and aggregate it in code, counting against what was asked; functions saved in its agent_helpers.py are available in every call. IN SCOPE: `page`, `context`, `browser` are Playwright's sync API (page.goto, page.locator(...).click()/fill(), page.get_by_role(...), page.wait_for_selector, page.evaluate; page.wait_for_timeout(ms) ends early once the page is quiet). To see a page, print(snapshot()): its elements with [IDs] and the structure around them (snapshot(contains="text") narrows it to the matches and their groups); act(("click", "0-42"), ("fill", "0-7", "Ada"), ("select", "0-9", "Tech"), ("check", "0-3"), ("press", "0-7", "Enter")) acts by those IDs and settles; take a new snapshot after a page changes (old IDs are refused). settle() waits for what an action started (navigation, requests, a changing DOM). Other helpers: new_tab(url) opens a tab and makes it `page`, goto_url(url), wait_for_load(), page_info() (url, title, viewport, scroll), js(expr) evaluates JavaScript and returns its value, fill_input(selector, text), click_at_xy(x, y), capture_screenshot() saves a PNG in the workspace and prints its path, show_screenshot() (full=True for the whole page) attaches a screenshot to this result for you to see when layout, images or canvas matter more than text, cdp('Domain.method', **params) sends raw CDP (cdp('Accessibility.getFullAXTree')['nodes'] lists every element: filter it in Python before printing), list_tabs(), switch_tab(id), ensure_real_tab(), answer_dialogs("accept") before an action that opens a native alert/confirm/prompt (dialogs are dismissed otherwise), wait_for_network_idle(), browser_events(). Each result lists what the tabs reported since the previous call: dialogs with their answers, console errors, page errors. Actions wait 5 s for their element (pass timeout= for a slower one). Login walls: never guess credentials; browser_vault types a login the user saved (list them first), otherwise ask the user.
browser_exec.name: browser_exec

code.description: Python to run against the browser. Use print(...) for anything you need back

session.description: A named browser of its own (its own tabs, cookies and profile) for work that must not share the default one; reuse the name on every related call

timeout.description: Seconds the code may run (optional; the call's budget otherwise)

browser_vault.description: Use a login the user saved, without seeing it: list the sites that have one, or fill one into the browser's current tab (it must be on that site) by naming the username and password fields (snapshot IDs or CSS selectors) and, optionally, what to click to submit. The values are typed for you and never shown to you; never ask the user for a password the vault holds, and never type one yourself.
browser_vault.name: browser_vault

action.description: list: the sites with a saved login; fill: type one into the current tab

login.description: fill: the site whose login to use, as list names it (e.g. https://shop.example.com)

password.description: fill: the password field, by snapshot ID or CSS selector

session.description: The named browser, as browser_exec's session (omit for the default one)

submit.description: fill: what to click after filling (optional), by snapshot ID or CSS selector

username.description: fill: the username field, by snapshot ID ("0-12") or CSS selector

edit.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.
edit.name: edit

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

find.description: Search for files by glob pattern. Returns matching file paths relative to the search directory. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 1000 results or 50KB (whichever is hit first).
find.name: find

path.description: Directory to search in (default: current directory)

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files, e.g. '*.ts', '**/*.json', or 'src/**/*.spec.ts'

git_commit.description: Stage every change in the workspace and create a git commit.
git_commit.name: git_commit

grep.description: Search file contents for a pattern. Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 100 matches or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Long lines are truncated to 500 chars.
grep.name: grep

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (default: 0)

glob.description: Filter files by glob pattern, e.g. '*.ts' or '**/*.spec.ts'

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 100)

literal.description: Treat pattern as literal string instead of regex (default: false)

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: current directory)

ls.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Includes dotfiles. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).
ls.name: ls

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default: 500)

note_for_session.description: Keep a lesson for the rest of this session: it is in your instructions from the next run on.
note_for_session.name: note_for_session

content.description: The lesson, as an instruction to yourself (e.g. "Run tests with make test, not pytest")

read.description: Read the contents of a file. Output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.
read.name: read

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

remember.description: Store a durable fact in long-term memory (append-only, safe to retry).
remember.name: remember

write.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.
write.name: write

content.description: Content to write to the file

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)
